title: Voyager 1 vs Parker Solar Probe vs Light | Speed Comparison #shorts
description_hook: From Voyager 1 at about 61,000 km/h to light at about 1.08 billion km/h: the fastest things, ranked.

items.name: VOYAGER 1
items.label: 61,000 KM/H
items.say: How fast can anything really go? Start with Voyager 1, leaving the solar system at about 61,000 km/h.
items.img: a small lonely space probe with a large white dish antenna drifting through the deep black emptiness beyond the planets, a faint distant star behind it

items.name: EARTH AROUND THE SUN
items.label: 107,000 KM/H
items.say: Earth itself. You're circling the Sun at about 107,000 km/h, sitting still.
items.img: the blue Earth seen from space sweeping along its orbit, a bright Sun far off to one side, a faint curved motion trail behind it

items.name: PARKER SOLAR PROBE
items.label: 700,000 KM/H
items.say: Parker Solar Probe, the fastest human-made object: about 700,000 km/h.
items.img: a compact spacecraft behind a dark round heat shield skimming close past a blazing solar surface, streaks of hot plasma flowing by

items.name: SUN AROUND GALAXY
items.label: 720,000 KM/H
items.say: But the whole solar system circles the galaxy at about 720,000 km/h. One lap takes about 230 million years.
items.img: a vast spiral galaxy seen from above with a single tiny glowing star marked by a soft halo far out in one of its arms

items.name: LIGHT
items.label: 1.08 BILLION KM/H
items.say: Light. About 1.08 billion km/h. Off the chart.
items.img: a single razor-thin beam of pure white light shooting straight through black space, stars blurred into streaks along its path

items.name: SUNLIGHT
items.say: And even light is slow. Sunlight needs about 8 minutes to reach you. The Sun you see is the past.
items.img: warm golden sunlight pouring through a gap in clouds over a quiet empty field at sunset, a lone figure from behind looking up at the Sun

gumi.say: Gumi's verdict: you're already faster than Voyager. Just by sitting there.
